## Natural history notes

A medium-sized nocturnal bird characterized by its mottled gray, brown, and black plumage, short legs, long wings, and wide mouth fringed with bristles for catching insects. In Florida, it is mostly associated with dry open woodlands, pine forests, scrub, forest edges, and wooded clearings, where its camouflage allows it to rest on the ground or low branches during the day. It feeds mainly on moths, beetles, mosquitoes, and other flying insects, foraging at dusk, night, and dawn and often detected by its repetitive “whip-poor-will” call.
